open_points.subject: FlowEdge guard-skip propagation
open_points.question: Does “skipped node” mean only a node recorded `skipped_by_guard`, or also one recorded `upstream_failed`; consequently, does `upstream_failed` propagate transitively through downstream nodes or become `skipped_by_guard` after one hop?
options: Both non-executed statuses count as skipped, so a node fed only by an `upstream_failed` node becomes `skipped_by_guard`
Both count as skipped, but the stated `upstream_failed` precedence makes the downstream node `upstream_failed`
open_points.default_guess: Treat `upstream_failed` as transitively propagated and let it win over `skipped_by_guard`.

open_points.subject: FlowEdge skipping of mapped nodes
open_points.text: A node one of whose input ports can no longer receive a value, because every edge into that port is disabled by its guard or comes from a skipped node, is not executed and is recorded `skipped_by_guard`
open_points.question: For a mapped node, is inability to receive a value evaluated for the whole node or separately for each `map_index`, and what happens when only some mapped elements are disabled or come from skipped upstream executions?
options: Skip only the affected mapped executions and retain outputs from the others
Skip the entire mapped node if any mapped element cannot receive a value
A mapped upstream node always produces one aggregate value, so partial skipping cannot occur
open_points.default_guess: Evaluate skipping per `map_index`, recording only affected elements as `skipped_by_guard`.
